note: Typed tool signatures for the state solver. Atoms: see atoms[]; entity atoms apply per entity. from_inputs: output atom <- source input slot (pass-through). makes_true: the tool sets the atom from its prompt, settings or model. not_specified: no guarantee; no solver credit. dropped: input atoms whose output atom is not_specified (PRD rule; atoms replaced from another slot are not listed). For video and image outputs, from_inputs + makes_true + not_specified cover every atom in scope. inputs[] lists media and prompt slots; numeric and enum params are in settings_that_set_atoms. basis: documented/inferred per magic-hour-tools.json maintains/mutates; mixed = both. Added tools carry a provider field; their specs are by design, not from docs.

atoms.definition: Who the entity is: face and recognizable likeness (for a product or logo: its brand identity).
Hair and head shape outside the face.
Body build, skin and proportions.
Clothing and accessories the entity wears.
Facial expression and eye gaze.
Body and head pose, and the motion or action over time.
Mouth motion matches the speech_audio track.
Voice timbre and speaking manner of the entity.
Setting and environment behind the entities.
Light direction, quality and colour on the scene.
Objects in the scene that are not entities or wardrobe.
Framing, shot size, angle and camera motion.
Visual rendering: art style, palette, colour grade.
On-screen text and graphic overlays: captions, titles, logos.
Spoken-word audio: words, language, timing.
Music track.
Sound effects and ambient sound.
Output media: image, video, audio or data.
Length in seconds.
Aspect ratio.
Pixel dimensions.
Frames per second.

signatures.nature: Generates motion that starts from a still frame and fills the time to an optional end frame, guided by a natural-language prompt. The prompt can steer subject action, expression, camera moves (pan, zoom, orbit) and environmental effects (wind, weather, light changes); it can likely animate an element that appears, fades or moves within the frame, with approximate timing only. It cannot keep exact on-screen text or pixel-exact logos, gives no alpha or transparency, gives no frame-exact timing, and the subject's identity can drift in later frames.

from_inputs.identity: assets.image_file_path (t=0; assets.end_image_file_path at t=end when given)
from_inputs.head_hair: assets.image_file_path (t=0; assets.end_image_file_path at t=end when given)
from_inputs.body: assets.image_file_path (t=0; assets.end_image_file_path at t=end when given)
from_inputs.wardrobe: assets.image_file_path (t=0; assets.end_image_file_path at t=end when given)
from_inputs.background: assets.image_file_path (t=0; assets.end_image_file_path at t=end when given)
from_inputs.lighting: assets.image_file_path (t=0; assets.end_image_file_path at t=end when given)
from_inputs.props: assets.image_file_path (t=0; assets.end_image_file_path at t=end when given)
from_inputs.style: assets.image_file_path (t=0; assets.end_image_file_path at t=end when given)

signatures.notes: First frame = input image [inferred]; end frame [documented]; motion and camera from prompt [documented]. Identity can drift in later frames [inferred]. aspect follows input image [inferred]. audio=true adds model audio with no content control, so no layer atom gets credit.

signatures.nature: Generates a complete new video clip from a natural-language prompt, with no prior image or video. The prompt can steer any visual content: entities, action, setting, lighting, weather, camera moves, transitions within the shot and art style; optional reference images may set subject identity (field semantics undocumented). It cannot reproduce a specific real person or brand without a reference, does not keep characters consistent across separate calls, renders text and logos unreliably, and gives no alpha or frame-exact timing; audio=true gives uncontrolled audio.
signatures.notes: Maintains nothing. Without references, the prompt sets identity only for a described generic entity; a real person needs a reference image. references semantics undocumented. Cross-call consistency not guaranteed. audio=true gives uncontrolled audio.

signatures.nature: Animates a single portrait photo so the face speaks a supplied audio track, moving lips, head and expression in sync with the audio. In prompted mode a prompt can also change background, camera and gesture, at slightly lower likeness; realistic mode keeps the photo's scene and framing. It needs a clear frontal face, accepts no text script (speech must exist as audio first), does little body or scene motion in realistic mode, and caps output at 720p.
signatures.notes: Likeness kept in realistic mode [documented]; prompted mode lowers likeness and lets the prompt change background and camera [documented]. Background, framing and audio pass-through [inferred]. Needs a clear frontal face. No text input: make speech with AI Voice Generator first.

signatures.nature: Re-animates only the mouth region of a person in an existing video so the lips match a new audio track; everything else in the frames stays. It has no prompt; settings only pick the time range, frame-rate cap and quality tier. It cannot change the voice, words, expression beyond the mouth, or any visual content, and quality drops with profile faces, occlusion, extreme head motion, several speakers or audio and video of different lengths.
signatures.notes: assets.youtube_url can replace the video file. Lip motion [documented]. Video content kept and audio replaced [inferred]. The input voice comes with the audio and can mismatch the person's identity. Best with one frontal speaker; audio and video of similar length.

signatures.nature: Replaces the face region of one or more people in an existing video with a face from a reference image, keeping the original expression, head motion and lighting. It has no prompt; settings pick all-faces or per-face mapping and the model version. It does not change hair, head shape, body, wardrobe, voice or scene, and quality drops with small faces, occlusion or extreme head motion; v1 keeps identity weakly.
signatures.notes: assets.youtube_url can replace the video file. Face identity, expression, head motion, lighting [documented]. Body, pose, background, camera, audio [inferred]. head_hair stays from the video, so a full likeness may need Character Replace. voice stays from the video. individual-faces needs Face Detection first. v2 keeps identity better.

signatures.nature: Re-renders every frame of an existing video in a new visual style (preset art style plus optional prompt), keeping the original motion, structure, timing and camera. The style and prompt can steer look, palette, colour grade and rendering medium (anime, oil paint, 3D, cyberpunk). It does not add, remove or move content, can break on-screen text and drift identity detail, degrades with fast motion or unstable lighting, and halves frame rate by default; audio pass-through is undocumented.
signatures.notes: assets.youtube_url can replace the video file. Motion and structure [documented]; framing and camera [inferred]. Repaints every frame: text may break, identity detail may drift [inferred]. Audio pass-through undocumented: mux the source audio back. Not for content changes.

signatures.nature: Edits an existing video clip from a natural-language instruction, re-generating the regions or properties the prompt names and carrying the rest from the source. The prompt can add, remove or replace objects, recolour, change wardrobe, background, lighting, weather or style; it can likely handle other local visual changes a prompt can describe. It is weak with several unrelated edits in one call and on fast-moving details, does not guarantee text or audio pass-through, gives no precise timing, and limits clip length per model (3-45 s).
signatures.notes: Changes objects, colours, scene details, style named in the prompt [documented]. Credit only for the atoms the prompt names; atoms the prompt does not name carry from the video [inferred]. One edit per call. Generative re-render: text and audio pass-through not guaranteed.

signatures.nature: Translates the speech in an existing video into a target language and replaces the spoken audio (documented); keeping the visuals, voice timbre and lip re-sync is inferred and unverified. Its only steering setting is the target language. It does not translate on-screen text, does not change any visual content, and accepts clips of 1-30 s only.
signatures.notes: Only spoken language is documented. Visuals, identity, voice timbre and lip re-sync are inferred and unverified (no tool guide page). On-screen text is kept but not translated. 1-30 s clips.

signatures.nature: Generates a stylized morphing animation frame by frame from a prompt or audio, with an optional start image as the first frame only. Presets steer art style and camera effect (zoom, pan, tilt, audio-synced moves), the prompt steers scene content, and transition speed sets how fast content morphs. It does not give photoreal continuous motion, does not keep a subject's identity across the clip, and cannot render exact text or logos.
signatures.notes: assets.youtube_url can replace the audio file. Start image = first frame only [documented]; content morphs over time, so image atoms get no credit across the clip. Style and camera from presets [documented]. Audio kept as the track [inferred]; audio must cover end_seconds. Morphing look, not photoreal motion.

signatures.nature: Generates video whose visuals and timing follow an audio track, with an optional reference image as the initial frame and an optional prompt for scene and style. The prompt can steer setting, props, style, action and camera. Lip sync to speech is not documented, identity is guaranteed only at the first frame, a prompt that conflicts with the reference image degrades output, and audio pass-through is unverified.
signatures.notes: Timing follows audio [documented]; reference image = initial frame [documented]. Audio kept in output [inferred, unverified]. Lip sync to speech is not documented. Without an image, entity atoms come from the prompt with no identity guarantee. Prompt conflicting with the image degrades output.

signatures.nature: Replaces the main person in an existing video with a character from a reference image, keeping the scene, background and motion (replace mode); animate mode instead transfers the video's motion onto the reference character. Settings pick the mode, model and which person (point selection, wan-animate only). It has no prompt for scene or style changes, breaks under occlusion, needs point selection when several people appear, limits kling-3.0 clips to 3-10 s (replace), and does not document audio pass-through.
signatures.notes: Signature is for style.mode=replace. Scene, background, motion kept [documented]; character appearance from image [documented]. speech_sync from video [inferred]. Audio pass-through undocumented. Pick the person with point selection when many people.

animate.notes: Motion from the video moves the character image.

signatures.nature: Transcribes the speech in an existing video and burns styled captions into the frames; all other content passes through. Templates or a custom config steer font, size, colours, stroke and position. It cannot write arbitrary text unrelated to the speech, has no language setting, gives no SRT/VTT file, and loses accuracy with noise, music or several speakers.
signatures.notes: Adds burned-in captions from a transcript of the video's speech_audio [documented]. Existing text and all other atoms kept [inferred]. No language parameter; no SRT export; noise and music reduce accuracy.

signatures.nature: Generates a complete new still image from a natural-language prompt, with no input image. The prompt can steer any visual content, composition, lighting and style, and tool presets target logos, posters and thumbnails. It cannot reproduce a specific real person or exact brand asset, does not keep identity consistent across calls, renders exact text unreliably, and gives no transparency.
signatures.notes: Maintains nothing. Identity only for a described generic entity; not consistent across calls [inferred]. Some style.tool presets (logo, poster, thumbnail) render text, but text is not in the spec, so no text credit.

signatures.nature: Edits one input image, or combines up to 10, from a natural-language instruction; it re-generates what the prompt names and carries the rest from the first image. The prompt can change wardrobe, expression, pose, background, lighting, props, camera framing and style, and can take elements from extra reference images. It is weak with several edits in one call, can drift a person's identity, does not reliably write or keep exact text or pixel-exact logos, and gives no transparency.

from_inputs.identity: assets.image_file_paths[0] (or image_file_paths[n] when the prompt says so)
from_inputs.head_hair: assets.image_file_paths[0] (or image_file_paths[n] when the prompt says so)
from_inputs.body: assets.image_file_paths[0] (or image_file_paths[n] when the prompt says so)

signatures.notes: General editor. Credit only for the atoms the prompt names; atoms the prompt does not name carry from image_file_paths[0] [inferred]. Can compose atoms from extra reference images [documented]. Identity can drift [inferred]. aspect_ratio=auto follows input. Text is not in the spec, so text carries and gets no credit. One edit per call.

signatures.nature: Replaces the face region of one or more people in a target image with a face from a source image, keeping expression, lighting, pose and scene. It has no prompt; settings pick all-faces or per-face mapping. It does not change hair, head shape, body or wardrobe, fails when no source face is found, and degrades with small or obscured faces, extreme angles or lighting mismatch.
signatures.notes: Face identity, expression, lighting [documented]. Pose, body, hair, background [inferred]. Output resolution is plan-capped. head_hair stays from the target: use Head Swap for hair.

signatures.nature: Places the whole head (face, hair, head shape) from one image onto the body in another image, keeping the body, pose and scene. It has no prompt; one setting caps resolution. It does not change body, wardrobe or scene, and degrades with angle, lighting or proportion mismatch, hair, hands or hats that cover the head, and cropped heads.
signatures.notes: Body, pose, scene kept [documented]. Whole head with face and hair from head image [documented]. expression from head image and text from body image [inferred].

signatures.nature: Places the person from one image into a scene image, replacing the scene's person and keeping the scene's background, composition and lighting. It has no prompt; only resolution is set. The pose may adapt to the scene without control, and it degrades with occlusion, pose, angle or lighting mismatch and low-quality inputs.
signatures.notes: Scene and person appearance kept [documented]. Pose can adapt to the scene [inferred], so pose_action is the tool's own. Lighting from scene [inferred].

signatures.nature: Dresses the person in an image with a garment from a reference image (virtual try-on), changing only the selected clothing region. A setting picks the region: full outfit, upper body or lower body. It cannot design clothing from text, does not change pose, face, lighting or background, and degrades when arms cover the clothing, lighting is poor or the background is busy.

from_inputs.wardrobe: assets.garment_file_path (region per garment_type; other regions from person)

signatures.notes: Pose, lighting, background [documented]; face identity [inferred]. Crossed arms and busy backgrounds degrade.

signatures.nature: Re-generates a photo of one person as a professional headshot, keeping facial identity and replacing background, attire, lighting and framing. An optional prompt steers background, attire, lighting and style. It needs exactly one detectable face, does not keep hair, expression, pose or props from the input, and degrades with sunglasses, masks or profiles.
signatures.notes: Keeps facial identity only [documented]. Sets background, attire, lighting, framing [documented]. Needs exactly one face. Hair and expression not specified.

signatures.nature: Adjusts the face in an image with numeric sliders for expression, eye gaze, mouth shape and head pose, keeping identity, lighting and scene. It has no prompt; each slider moves one facial feature by a set amount. It cannot change anything outside the face and head pose, and large slider values look unnatural.
signatures.notes: Expression, gaze, head pose by sliders [documented]. Identity, lighting [documented]; background, clothing [inferred]. pose_action here = head pose only. Large slider values look unnatural.

signatures.nature: Increases the resolution of an image 2x or 4x and recovers detail, keeping content, composition and aspect. Mode steers how much detail it invents (preserve, balanced, creative); creative mode accepts a prompt and can reinterpret detail and style. It cannot recover detail that is not there, amplifies JPEG artifacts and is weak on text-heavy images.
signatures.notes: Content and composition kept [documented]; aspect [inferred]. creative mode can reinterpret detail and style. Weak on text-heavy images.

signatures.nature: Cuts out the main subject of an image and outputs it with a transparent alpha background, or composites it onto a supplied background image. It has no prompt. It does not relight the subject to match a new background, loses props and text in the old background, and degrades with fine hair on busy backgrounds, transparent objects and low subject-background contrast.
signatures.notes: Subject cutout [documented]; dimensions kept [inferred]. No relight: subject lighting can mismatch the new background. props and text in the old background are lost; a held prop counts as subject only when the cutout keeps it. Fine hair and low contrast degrade.

signatures.nature: Adds realistic colour to a black-and-white or grayscale photo, keeping content and structure. It has no prompt or settings, so the palette is the model's choice. It cannot apply a chosen colour grade or style, and results vary on complex scenes and damaged scans.
signatures.notes: Adds colour (style: palette) [documented]. Content and structure kept [inferred].

signatures.nature: Generates a short new animation (gif, mp4 or webm) from a prompt of up to 500 characters, with no input image. The prompt can steer any visual content and style of the loop. It has no duration, aspect or resolution control, no audio, cannot use a reference for identity, and renders text unreliably.
signatures.notes: No image input; no duration control [documented]. Output is gif, mp4 or webm (an image project). No audio.

signatures.nature: Writes panel text for a topic onto a fixed meme template image. The topic steers the text; a setting picks the template. It cannot use the user's own images or entities, cannot change the template's visuals, and gives weak text for vague topics.
signatures.notes: Template image is fixed by preset [documented]; the tool writes panel text for the topic [documented]. Visual atoms come from the template preset, not the user's assets.

signatures.nature: Generates an artistic QR code image that encodes a given URL or text, rendered in a chosen preset or free-text art style. The style prompt steers the look and background. Scannability is a goal, not a guarantee (busy or low-contrast styles can break it), and it does not place readable text, logos or entities.
signatures.notes: text here = encoded payload, not readable glyphs. Scannability is a goal; test it. Busy styles can break scanning.

signatures.nature: Converts a text script into speech in one of 1266 preset voices. The script sets the words and the voice preset sets timbre and manner. It cannot clone a real person's voice, has no language setting, makes no music or sound effects, and its duration follows the script length (max 1000 characters).
signatures.notes: Script text kept as the words [documented]. voice from a preset only; a real person's voice needs AI Voice Cloner. No language parameter; duration follows text length. Not in hosted MCP.

signatures.nature: Speaks a new text script in the voice cloned from an audio sample, keeping the sample's timbre, intonation and speaking patterns. The script sets the words. It needs one clean speaker of at least 3 s, degrades with noisy or multi-speaker samples, has no language setting, and makes no music or sound effects.
signatures.notes: Timbre, intonation, speaking patterns from the sample [documented]; new words from the prompt [documented]. Sample: one clean speaker, >= 3 s. Not in hosted MCP.

signatures.nature: Analyses an image or video and returns a list of the faces it finds as crops. A confidence threshold steers how many faces it keeps. It changes no media; its only use is to feed per-face mappings to Face Swap Video and Face Swap Photo.

from_inputs.identity: assets.target_file_path (one face crop per detected entity)

signatures.notes: Analysis only; the input media does not change. Output faces[] feed face_mappings[].original_face in Face Swap Video and Face Swap Photo. Accepts image or video.

signatures.nature: Returns upload URLs and file paths so local files can be used as inputs to other tools. It changes no content; the uploaded file keeps all its properties. Uploads expire after 7 days.
signatures.notes: No atom changes. Gives file_path values; the uploaded file keeps all its atoms. Uploads kept 7 days.

signatures.nature: Intended: generates a music track from a text brief; no provider is bound yet. The brief and settings are intended to steer mood, tempo and duration. Intended to make music only: no speech, voice or sound effects, and no guarantee of beat-exact sync to picture.
signatures.notes: Type music_score: (mood, duration) -> AudioTrack, from 05-solver.md. Binding decided at execution.

signatures.nature: Intended: generates sound effects or ambient sound from a text brief, with cue times; no provider is bound yet. The brief is intended to steer the kind of sound and the cue times its placement. Intended to make sound effects only: no speech or music.
signatures.notes: Binding decided at execution.

signatures.nature: Intended: deterministically draws given text onto an image or video (e.g. ffmpeg drawtext), with no generative model. Settings set font, size, colour, position and start and end times exactly, so text is pixel-exact and timing is frame-exact. It does not change any other content and cannot make text interact with the scene (no relighting, occlusion or 3D tracking).
signatures.notes: base can be image or video. Adds the text to the existing text layer; all other atoms pass through. ffmpeg drawtext.

signatures.nature: Intended: deterministically composites a supplied logo image onto an image or video (e.g. ffmpeg overlay), with no generative model. Settings set position, scale and start and end times exactly, so the logo stays pixel-exact. It does not change any other content and cannot animate the logo beyond placement and timing unless combined with fade or transform.
signatures.notes: The logo joins the text/overlay layer; all other atoms pass through. ffmpeg overlay.

signatures.nature: Intended: deterministically changes the opacity of a whole image or video, or of one overlay layer, over a time range (fade in, fade out, fade to black). Settings set target layer, curve and start and end times exactly. It does not change content; it cannot fade one element inside the generated pixels, only a whole frame or a separate layer.
signatures.notes: Changes opacity of a layer or the whole frame over time. No atom covers opacity or visibility timing: open gap in the vocabulary.

signatures.nature: Intended: deterministically translates, scales or rotates the whole frame or one overlay layer, optionally over time (digital zoom, pan, Ken Burns move). Settings set the values exactly. It makes no new pixels: a zoom-in loses resolution, it cannot reveal content outside the frame, and it gives no parallax or true 3D camera motion.
signatures.notes: On the whole frame it sets framing (camera). On an overlay layer it sets text placement. Pixels otherwise pass through.

signatures.nature: Intended: deterministically crops or pads a frame to a target aspect and resolution. Settings set the crop box, target aspect, target resolution and padding exactly. It makes no new pixels: cropping can cut off text or entities at the edges, and padding adds plain borders, not new scene content.
signatures.notes: Crop or pad to a target aspect. Can cut off text or entities at the edges.

signatures.nature: Intended: deterministically cuts a video to a start and end time, keeping the content of the kept range. Settings set the times exactly. It does not change content, speed or order, and cannot extend a clip beyond its source length.
signatures.notes: Keeps the atoms of the kept time range.

signatures.nature: Intended: deterministically joins video segments in time, in a set order, with optional transitions; each segment keeps its own content in its time range. Settings set order and transition type. It does not change segment content, needs segments that share aspect, resolution and frame rate (or a crop_reformat first), and cannot make a seamless continuous shot from unrelated segments.

from_inputs.identity: segments[i] over its time range [t_i, t_i + duration_i]
from_inputs.head_hair: segments[i] over its time range [t_i, t_i + duration_i]

from_inputs.pose_action: segments[i] over its time range [t_i, t_i + duration_i]
from_inputs.speech_sync: segments[i] over its time range [t_i, t_i + duration_i]
from_inputs.voice: segments[i] over its time range [t_i, t_i + duration_i]
from_inputs.background: segments[i] over its time range [t_i, t_i + duration_i]
from_inputs.lighting: segments[i] over its time range [t_i, t_i + duration_i]
from_inputs.props: segments[i] over its time range [t_i, t_i + duration_i]
from_inputs.camera: segments[i] over its time range [t_i, t_i + duration_i]
from_inputs.style: segments[i] over its time range [t_i, t_i + duration_i]
from_inputs.text: segments[i] over its time range [t_i, t_i + duration_i]
from_inputs.speech_audio: segments[i] over its time range [t_i, t_i + duration_i]
from_inputs.music: segments[i] over its time range [t_i, t_i + duration_i]
from_inputs.sfx: segments[i] over its time range [t_i, t_i + duration_i]

from_inputs.frame_rate: segments[i] over its time range [t_i, t_i + duration_i]

signatures.notes: Join in time. duration = sum of segment durations (minus transition overlap). Each segment keeps all its atoms in its own time range; the solver splits a goal into per-scene sub-goals and joins them here. Segments must share aspect, resolution, frame_rate, or a crop_reformat runs first.

signatures.nature: Intended: deterministically mixes speech, music and sound-effect tracks and attaches them to a video, keeping all visuals. Settings set gain, ducking and offset exactly. It makes no new audio or visuals, and it does not create lip sync: speech matches the mouth only when the speech track is the audio the video was lip-synced to.
signatures.notes: Join in layers. Each layer keeps the atoms of its own input; the solver splits a goal into visual, speech, music and sfx sub-goals and joins them here. speech_sync holds only when the speech slot is the same audio the video was lip-synced to. Mix only (no video) gives an audio output.
